settings.heading: Ingredients
settings.content:
Purified spring water, organic virgin coconut oil, plant-based emulsifying wax, palm stearic, grapefruit seed extract, organic beeswax, organic red palm oil.

Variation essential oils:

  • Coconut Breeze: organic coconut oil extract
  • Lavender & Rose: lavender, rose, roman chamomile, geranium

settings.heading: Details
settings.content:
Thick, but it does not sit on you. It goes on like butter and works in — heavy enough for rough spots, without the slick film.

Built for the places a lotion does not fix. Hands, knees, legs and feet, extreme dryness, post-shower routines, overnight.

A little goes a long way. A tiny bit covers more than a pump of lotion does.

Honest trade-off. Closer to a balm than a pump cream. It firms in cold weather because beeswax does. Not a fast-absorbing daytime lotion.

settings.heading: How to Use
settings.content: Warm a small amount between your fingers to soften, then apply to dry skin. Best at night for overnight occlusion or after a bath. Pay extra attention to elbows, hands, and feet — areas where most lotions don't last long enough.

settings.title: Organic Beeswax
settings.text: Moisture-lock barrier. Beeswax forms a breathable barrier that locks moisture in without sealing pores shut. Its long-chain fatty acids and esters create a flexible film that holds skin's own water content while still allowing gas exchange. Cheap barrier waxes are shelf-stable forever and fully occlusive. We pay more for beeswax.

settings.title: Organic Virgin Coconut Oil
settings.text: Fatty-acid nourishment. Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil keeps its full lauric acid content — roughly 50% of its fatty acid profile. The medium-chain fatty acids absorb into the skin barrier rather than sitting on top. Refined coconut oil is cheaper and uniform batch-to-batch because the lab strips the variation out, along with most of the lauric acid.

settings.title: Organic Red Palm Oil
settings.text: Vitamin E and beta-carotene source. Unrefined red palm oil contributes naturally occurring vitamin E and tocotrienols — antioxidants that nourish the skin barrier the cream is built to protect. The deep red-orange color comes from the carotenoids, not added pigment. RSPO-certified sourcing.

settings.heading: Why is this cream so thick?
settings.row_content: This is closer to a balm than a pump cream. Beeswax and palm stearic give it the body — both are doing real work as a moisture-lock barrier and a natural thickener. Conventional creams use synthetic thickeners and silicones to feel light and fast-absorbing. We left those out. Warm a small amount between your fingers before applying and it softens immediately.

settings.heading: Why does it firm up in cold weather?
settings.row_content: Beeswax and coconut oil both firm up below about 76°F — that's the ingredients behaving the way real ingredients behave. Conventional creams stay uniform across temperatures because synthetic thickeners hold the texture artificially. If your jar feels firm, scoop a small amount and warm it between your fingers; it softens in seconds.

settings.heading: Can I use this on my face?
settings.row_content: Most customers use this as a body cream, on hands and feet, or on dry patches — it's heavier than a daytime facial moisturizer. If your face is extremely dry, a thin layer at night can work well. We'd suggest patch-testing first if you have reactive skin, even though we formulated this without common irritants like lanolin or synthetic fragrance.

settings.heading: Why use beeswax as the barrier?
settings.row_content: The usual barrier waxes seal skin without feeding it — cheap, shelf-stable forever, and fully occlusive. Beeswax forms a breathable barrier instead. It locks moisture in while still allowing gas exchange at the molecular level. The trade-off is real: beeswax costs more, and the cream firms up in cold weather. We accept both.

settings.heading: Why is the cream tinted?
settings.row_content: The color comes from the unrefined red palm oil — beta-carotene and tocotrienols give it that red-orange tone. Refined palm oil is bleached white and stripped of those antioxidants. Since the antioxidants are why we're using palm oil at all, we use the unrefined version and accept the color. The Pure Unscented variation has the same tint for the same reason.

settings.heading: Is the unscented version actually fragrance-free?
settings.row_content: No essential oils are added to the Pure Unscented variation. You'll still detect a faint scent of beeswax and coconut — that's the ingredients themselves, not added fragrance. If you've reacted to "unscented" products in the past, that's often because they contain masking fragrance to neutralize a base odor. We don't use masking fragrance.

settings.heading: How long does a jar last?
settings.row_content: Grapefruit seed extract is our natural preservative — it inhibits bacterial and fungal growth without parabens or phenoxyethanol. Unopened, the cream is shelf-stable for about 12 months. Once opened, use within 6 months and keep the lid sealed. Use clean fingers or a small spatula to scoop; introducing water or contaminants will shorten shelf life.

settings.heading: Is the red palm oil sustainably sourced?
settings.row_content: Yes — we use RSPO-certified red palm oil. The Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil certifies the palm comes from operations meeting strict standards: no deforestation, no peatland conversion, fair labor. The "red" matters too — refined palm oil is cheaper but the refining strips out the carotenoids and tocotrienols we use it for. Unrefined keeps the antioxidants intact.
